lines.trans: Goodbye!

meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Refers both to physical foundations and to the base of a recipe or argument.

examples.text: أساس الكيكة لازم يكون خفيف ومستوي منيح.
examples.trans: The base of the cake needs to be light and baked well.

examples.text: الثقة هي أساس كل شغلنا بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: Trust is the foundation of all our work in the kitchen.

meanings.note: The color black.

examples.trans: I wore a black shirt.

examples.text: اشتريت جاكيت أسود دافي عشان الشتا.
examples.trans: I bought a warm black jacket for the winter.

meanings.note: A sigh of dismay or tiredness, a little like English 'oof' or 'ugh'.

examples.trans: Oof, I forgot the key at home!
Ugh, it's hot today.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from إسفنج (sponge); commonly describes light cakes.

examples.text: عملت سلمى كيكة إسفنجية خفيفة مع التوت.
examples.trans: Salma made a light sponge cake with berries.
Fresh bread has a soft and spongy texture.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait just a minute.

examples.text: استنى شوي، أنا نازل معك هسه!
examples.trans: Wait a second—I'm coming down with you right now!

meanings.note: Commonly refers to mulberries, which are popular in Jordan, or any berry.

examples.trans: Mulberry juice is very delicious in the summer.

examples.text: شجرة التوت بالحديقة صارت مليانة حبات سودة حلوة.
examples.trans: The mulberry tree in the garden is full of sweet dark berries now.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: The man who I saw yesterday.

examples.text: هذا المحل اللي اشترينا منه الكنافة الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: This is the shop where we bought the kunafa last week.

meanings.note: Frequently used with بـ as بانتظام (neatly, regularly).

examples.trans: Arrange the trays neatly on the table.
Suad waters the flowers in the garden regularly.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ب- before nouns ('in/with'); with pronoun suffixes in Levantine it takes the stem في-: فيي ('in me'), فيك ('in/to you m.'), فيكي ('in/to you f.'), فيه ('in him/it'), فيها ('in her/it'), فينا ('in us'), فيهم ('in them').

examples.trans: Welcome to Jasmine House!
My suitcase has a red ribbon in it.

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine adverbial phrase meaning 'at all' in negatives (ما شفته بالمرة) or 'altogether / completely'.

examples.trans: I did not rush the playing at all today.

examples.text: الموضوع هاد عملي بدون عاطفة بالمرة.
examples.trans: This matter is practical with zero sentiment at all.

meanings.note: Used to indicate the center of something or splitting something equally.

examples.trans: Split the apple in half.
Tin Two is placed right in the middle.

meanings.note: Describes doing an action without rushing.

examples.trans: The car was moving very slowly.

examples.text: عم يمضغ اللقمة ببطء وهو بفكر.
examples.trans: He is chewing the bite slowly while thinking.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'want / need', inflected with pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بده (he/it wants), بدها (she/it wants), بدنا (we want), بدكم (you pl. want), بدهم (they want).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Jam bread needs unsalted butter.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'without', used identically to MSA.

examples.trans: I like coffee without sugar.

examples.text: شرب القهوة بدون سكر مع قطعة بقلاوة.
examples.trans: He drank the coffee without sugar alongside a piece of baklava.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: After a plural verb, بعض means 'each other' (بننادي بعض 'we call each other').

examples.trans: We call each other by first name here.

examples.text: ما حكينا مع بعض من زمان.
examples.trans: We have not spoken with each other in a long time.

meanings.note: Active participle of the geminate verb تمّ.

examples.text: التذوق المضبوط بده هدوء تام بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: A proper tasting requires complete silence in the kitchen.

examples.text: كلامك إله معنى تام ومقنع كتير.
examples.trans: Your words make total sense and are very convincing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.trans: My brother's car is broken.
Where is the key belonging to the kitchen cupboard?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتخانق, بيتخانق).

examples.trans: We used to argue over the corner piece!
We fell out over selling the old house.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of Form V تذوق.

examples.text: اليوم عندنا تذوق لتلات كيكات مختلفة.
examples.trans: Today we have a tasting of three different cakes.

examples.text: التذوق المضبوط محتاج كاسة مي وشاي.
examples.trans: A proper tasting needs a glass of water and tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بترك, بيترك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف جنب الجرس؟
examples.trans: Who left this envelope by the bell?
Thank you for not leaving me in the rain.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Count to ten: one, two, three.

examples.text: رتبنا الصحون واحد تنين تلاتة عالطاولة.
examples.trans: We lined up the plates one, two, three on the table.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of لمّع ('to polish wood, brass, or shoes').

examples.text: بقي بس تلميع دواسات النحاس بقماشة ناعمة.
examples.trans: All that's left is polishing the brass pedals with a soft cloth.

examples.text: بعد التلميع رجع خشب الجوز يلمع زي المراية.
examples.trans: After polishing, the walnut wood shone like a mirror again.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for mouth, or the pouring spout of a pitcher/teapot.

examples.trans: The pitcher's spout is a little wide.
He laughed wholeheartedly.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: I only want two pieces, two are enough.

examples.text: جبنا كتابين تنين من رف الإعارة.
examples.trans: We brought two books from the lending shelf.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian expression to express surprise or ask for confirmation, like 'really?' or 'seriously!'.

examples.trans: Are you talking seriously?

examples.text: جد؟ لقيتوا المفتاح الضاع جوا المطبخ؟
examples.trans: Seriously? Did you find the lost key inside the kitchen?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجرب, بيجرب).

examples.trans: This sweater is clean and new — try it on.
We tried the new recipe and it turned out delicious.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حواجب.

examples.trans: Why did you knit your eyebrows like that?
He raised his eyebrow in surprise.

meanings.note: Describes citrus, yogurt, or tart flavours.

examples.text: كريمة الليمون طلعت حامضة زيادة عن اللزوم.
examples.trans: The lemon icing turned out too sour.

examples.text: التوت الأخضر بعده حامض قبل ما يستوي.
examples.trans: Green berries are still tart before they ripen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Save the formal talk for later.
That is kind, honest talk.

meanings.note: One of the most frequently used adjectives in Jordanian Arabic to mean beautiful, sweet, nice, or good.

examples.trans: This dress is very beautiful on you.

examples.text: طعم العسل مع قشر البرتقال حلو ومتوازن.
examples.trans: The taste of honey with orange peel is sweet and balanced.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خفيفة, plural: خفاف).

examples.trans: Coffee with milk and light sugar.
A light, tasty breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The weather today is very warm.

examples.text: الحليب الدافي بسكر الخميرة وبخليها تتفاعل.
examples.trans: Warm milk activates the yeast and helps it rise.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: What is your phone number?

examples.text: كل بطاقة إلها رقم متسلسل من واحد لعشرة.
examples.trans: Each card has a serial number from one to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I like black tea without sugar.
We sprinkled powdered sugar over the cake.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a knife. Can be pronounced 'sikkiin' or 'sikkiina'.

examples.trans: Bring the knife so we can cut the cake.

examples.text: قصينا الكيكة بسكينة رفيعة عشان تطلع مرتبة.
examples.trans: We cut the cake with a thin knife so it comes out neat.

meanings.note: Used with بـ (بسلاسة 'smoothly / effortlessly').

examples.text: بعد نقطة الزيت، الباب فتح بسلاسة.
examples.trans: After a drop of oil, the door swung open smoothly.

examples.text: نغمة دو بتطلع وبتنزل بكل سلاسة.
examples.trans: The C key rises and falls completely smoothly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمح, بيسمح).

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Allow me to pour the orange juice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: I like to drink tea after lunch.

examples.text: صبينا كاسات شاي ساخن مع ورق النعناع.
examples.trans: We poured glasses of hot tea with mint leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشبك, بيشبك).

examples.trans: Plug in Tariq's brass lamp.
We clipped the second sheet to the envelope.

meanings.note: Used constantly as بصراحة or bare صراحة ('honestly / to be frank').

examples.trans: Honestly, I loved the place very much.
Frankly, the coffee here is excellent.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صفوف.

examples.trans: We sat in the front row at the concert.
The chairs are arranged in two rows.

meanings.note: Broken plural صواني ('serving trays' or 'oven baking pans').

examples.text: جهزنا تلات صواني خبز عشان تدخل الفرن الفجر.
examples.trans: We prepped three trays of bread to go into the oven at dawn.

examples.text: نور حملت صينية الشاي بالنعنع للساحة.
examples.trans: Nour carried the mint tea tray out to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Very common Levantine verb meaning to stay, remain, or keep doing something.

examples.trans: He stayed at home and didn't go out.

examples.text: ضل الدفتر مفتوح عالطاولة طول الليل.
examples.trans: The notebook remained open on the table all night.

meanings.note: Active participle of طغى; in tasting contexts means a flavour or scent that overpowers everything else.

examples.text: طعمة الهيل كانت طاغية على نكهة الفانيليا.
examples.trans: The cardamom flavour was overpowering the vanilla note.

examples.text: اللون الأحمر طاغي على كل الرسومات.
examples.trans: The red colour dominates all the drawings.

meanings.note: Common everyday word for table.

examples.trans: Put the things on the table.

examples.text: طاولة المطبخ مليانة علب بهارات ومرطبانات.
examples.trans: The kitchen table is full of spice tins and jars.

meanings.note: Used for a coat of paint (طبقة دهان), a layer of pastry, or a building storey.

examples.text: الطبقة الأولى نشفت وصارت جاهزة للطبقة التانية.
examples.trans: The first coat has dried and is ready for the second coat.

examples.text: دهان المي بيكفيه طبقتين رقيقتين عشان يطلع ناعم.
examples.trans: Water-based paint only needs two thin coats to come out smooth.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Here is mint tea with honey.
Mountain honey tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة على الطاولة وبلشنا نحللها.
examples.trans: We laid the map on the table and began analysing it.

meanings.note: Preposition 'ala' with a third-person feminine pronoun suffix.

examples.trans: There is dust on it (the table).

examples.text: العلبة عليها ختم شمع وبصمة صغيرة.
examples.trans: The tin has a wax seal and a small stamp on it.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: The car is at the door.

examples.text: التقينا عند برج الساعة الساعة عشرة.
examples.trans: We met by the clock tower at ten o'clock.

meanings.note: After negation, ما ... غير means 'only / nothing except'.

examples.text: ما معي غير المعطف اللي علي!
examples.trans: I have nothing with me except the coat I have on!
There are only two valves on the shelf.

meanings.note: Used to describe an empty container or a person who has free time.

examples.trans: I am free today in the afternoon.

examples.text: الرف الفوقاني فاضي، بنقدر نحط العلبة عليه.
examples.trans: The top shelf is empty; we can put the tin on it.

meanings.note: Invariable culinary loanword treated grammatically as feminine in Jordanian recipes.

examples.text: حطي معلقة فانيليا صغيرة على خليط الكيك.
examples.trans: Put a small spoonful of vanilla into the cake batter.

examples.text: ريحة الفانيليا طالعة من المطبخ للدور التاني.
examples.trans: The scent of vanilla is drifting from the kitchen to the second floor.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أفران.

examples.text: لفائف القرفة طلعت من الفرن هلا.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
The bakery down the street bakes in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قاسية, plural: قاسيين).

examples.text: كان يعمل حاله قاسي خمس ثواني بس!
examples.trans: He used to act tough for just five seconds!
Amman's winter cold is sometimes harsh.

meanings.note: Defective noun on the faa'i pattern; drops final -y in indefinite nominative/genitive only in formal Arabic, kept as قاضي in Jordanian.

examples.trans: The judge asked to hear the two witnesses' statements.

examples.text: العم سالم معروف عند الجيران كأنه قاضي الحكيم.
examples.trans: Uncle Salem is known among the neighbours like a wise judge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قواعد.

examples.text: أول قاعدة: اشرب شاي سخن الصبح!
examples.trans: Rule one: drink hot tea in the morning!
The work rules here are simple and clear.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قراءات.

examples.trans: We put a brass reading lamp by the desk.
I love reading in the quiet courtyard.

meanings.note: Form II verb used both transitively ('bring the lamp closer') and intransitively ('come closer').

examples.text: قرب الفانوس شوي عشان أشوف القفل.
examples.trans: Bring the lantern a little closer so I can see the lock.
We pulled the chairs closer to the big table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقطع, بيقطع).

examples.text: جدي كان يقطع كيكة ليمون دافية.
examples.trans: My grandfather used to slice warm lemon cake.
Salma sliced the hot bread.

meanings.note: The beloved beverage, often Arabic coffee or Turkish-style, and by extension a coffee shop.

examples.trans: Would you drink coffee or tea?

examples.text: حضرنا فنجان قهوة بالهيل للضيوف باللوبي.
examples.trans: We prepared a cup of cardamom coffee for the guests in the lobby.

meanings.note: In baking and cooking, قوام specifically refers to the thickness, crumb, or consistency of a batter or cake.

examples.text: قوام الكيكة طلع طري ومتماسك بنفس الوقت.
examples.trans: The texture of the cake came out soft and firm at the same time.

examples.text: لازم نخفق البيض لحد ما يتقل قوامه.
examples.trans: We need to beat the eggs until their consistency thickens.

meanings.note: With بـ + الـ, بالقوة means 'by force / forcefully'.

examples.trans: She grabbed my hand forcefully.
Honesty gives us strength.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: The weather was cold yesterday.

examples.text: الطعم كان متوازن كتير بين العسل والليمون.
examples.trans: The flavour was very well balanced between the honey and lemon.

meanings.note: Placed AFTER the adjective or verb it intensifies: تقيلة كتير ('very heavy'), شكرا كتير ('thank you very much').

examples.trans: The smell is so good!
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Culinary noun used for كريمة الليمون ('lemon curd / cream') and pastry fillings.

examples.text: نور جهزت كريمة الليمون الصفرا للتارت.
examples.trans: Nour prepared the bright yellow lemon curd for the tarts.

examples.text: ريحة كريمة الليمون الطازة عبت المطبخ كله.
examples.trans: The aroma of fresh lemon curd filled the entire kitchen.

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.trans: I made a delicious chocolate cake.

examples.text: كيكة التوت اللي عملتها سلمى طلعت خفيفة وهشة.
examples.trans: The berry cake that Salma made turned out light and fluffy.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'no' or 'not', used exactly like Standard Arabic.

examples.trans: No, I don't want to go today.

examples.text: لا تنسوا تطفيوا الفرن بعد ما تخلصوا الخبيز.
examples.trans: Do not forget to turn off the oven after you finish baking.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: لابسة, plural: لابسين).

examples.trans: He is standing outside wearing a grey coat.
She is wearing a warm wool sweater.

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everything has to be just right!

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Conditional particle used for hypothetical or impossible situations (contrary-to-fact conditions).

examples.text: لو بعرف إنك جاي، كنت استنيتك.
examples.trans: If I knew you were coming, I would have waited for you.

examples.text: لو لقينا المفتاح بدري كنا فتحنا الصندوق امبارح.
examples.trans: If we had found the key earlier we would have opened the chest yesterday.

meanings.note: Literally means almonds, but heavily used in Jordanian youth slang to mean 'everything is perfect' or 'great'.

examples.trans: The situation is perfect, don't worry.

examples.text: زينت سلمى وش الكيكة بشرايح لوز محمص.
examples.trans: Salma decorated the top of the cake with toasted almond slices.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: I haven't eaten anything since the morning.

examples.text: ما عرفت إنه العلبة فيها طابق سري من تحت.
examples.trans: I did not know that the box had a secret compartment underneath.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ماشية, plural: ماشيين).

examples.trans: I saw my brother walking down this street.
Everything is going smoothly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مبينة, plural: مبينين).

examples.trans: The wooden train looks old and precious.
It looks like it is going to rain tonight.

meanings.note: Form VIII participle of اختلف; precedes plural nouns or follows singular nouns to indicate difference.

examples.text: كل صينية إلها رقم وطعم مختلف عن التانية.
examples.trans: Each tin has a different number and taste from the next.

examples.text: جربنا تلات طرق مختلفة لتسخين العسل.
examples.trans: We tried three different ways to warm the honey.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: مديرة). Plural: مدراء.

examples.trans: She became the permanent front-desk manager at the guesthouse.
The manager welcomed the new guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a glass jam, honey, or olive jar (dual مرطبانين, plural مرطبانات).

examples.trans: We lined the jars of jam and honey up on the shelf.
Open the new jar of honey for breakfast.

meanings.note: Form VIII participle from root س-و-ي. Means level/flat for surfaces, and 'well-cooked/ripe' for food.

examples.trans: Put it on a level surface.
The table isn't level, it wobbles.

meanings.note: Common defective verb for walking on foot or things running smoothly.

examples.text: ممنوع تمشي عكاحلك لحد بكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: You mustn't walk on your ankle until tomorrow morning.

examples.text: مشينا عالهدا بالساحة بعد ما وقفت المطر.
examples.trans: We walked gently across the courtyard after the rain stopped.

meanings.note: Pronounced mazbuut in Amman; means 'properly, accurately, that's right!'.

examples.trans: Let me speak with him properly!
What you say is one hundred percent right.

meanings.note: Form I sound verb describing chewing food carefully, especially during tasting.

examples.text: مضغ اللقمة على مهله عشان يميز البهارات.
examples.trans: He chewed the bite slowly so he could tell the spices apart.

examples.text: امضغ الأكل منيح قبل ما تبلعه.
examples.trans: Chew the food well before swallowing it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Conversational vocalization expressing either delight at tasty food or thoughtful hesitation.

examples.trans: Mmm, the smell of the cake in the oven is mouth-watering!

examples.text: ممم، خلينا نفكر شوي قبل ما نجاوب.
examples.trans: Hmm, let us think a moment before we answer.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Levantine equivalent for 'jayyida', feminine form.

examples.trans: The idea is very good.

examples.text: نتيجة التذوق طلعت منيحة وأحسن من المرة الأولى.
examples.trans: The tasting result came out good and better than the first time.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: موظفة). Plural: موظفين.

examples.trans: I am the new receptionist at the guesthouse.
All the staff here are helpful and friendly.

meanings.note: Traditional Levantine term for seasonal homemade pantry preserves such as olive oil, pickles, herbs, and jams.

examples.text: الجدة دايما بتحفظ مونة العسل والزعتر بالرف العالي.
examples.trans: Grandmother always keeps the honey and thyme pantry provisions on the top shelf.

examples.text: بيت المونة مليان مرطبانات مربى ومخلل.
examples.trans: The pantry room is full of jars of jam and pickles.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Form II verb (نظّف) with doubled middle radical; imperative نظّف / نظّفي.

examples.text: نظفوا الطاولة منيح قبل ما نحط الصواني.
examples.trans: Clean the table well before we set down the trays.

examples.text: مازن نظف العلبة المعدنية بقطعة قماش ناشفة.
examples.trans: Mazen cleaned the metal tin with a dry cloth.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation of هذا ('this/that').

examples.text: هادا الكتاب من أحلى الروايات اللي قرأتها هالسنة.
examples.trans: This book is one of the best novels I've read this year.

examples.text: مين جاب هادا الفانوس الحلو عالطاولة؟
examples.trans: Who brought this lovely lantern onto the table?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The morning quiet of the courtyard is very peaceful.
We talked the matter through calmly and patiently.

meanings.note: In baking, هش describes a tender, airy cake crumb or crisp pastry that melts lightly.

examples.text: الكيكة طلعت هشة وخفيفة متل الإسفنج.
examples.trans: The cake came out fluffy and light like a sponge.
Crumbly biscuits break easily in the tin.

meanings.note: Signature urban Jordanian/Levantine adverb for now (also spelled هلا in Jordan).

examples.text: هلق رح نفتح الصينية ونذوق أول قطعة.
examples.trans: Right now we will open the tin and taste the first piece.
We finished writing the notes just now.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: There is someone asking about you.

examples.text: اشتريت كتاب واحد بس من المعرض لأنه كان غالي.
examples.trans: I bought just one book from the fair because it was expensive.

meanings.note: Modern expressive exclamation of admiration or amazement, common among younger Jordanian speakers.

examples.text: واو! شكل الكيكة باللوز والعسل بجنن!
examples.trans: Wow! The honey-and-almond cake looks amazing!

examples.text: واو، كيف قدرت تحل اللغز بهالسرعة؟
examples.trans: Wow, how did you manage to solve the puzzle so fast?

meanings.note: The standard interrogative adverb for location in the dialect.

examples.trans: Where are you going?

examples.text: وين حطيت مفاتيح السيارة بعد ما رجعت من الشغل؟
examples.trans: Where did you put the car keys after you got back from work?

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.

meanings.note: Direction noun synonymous with شمال (left) in urban speech; frequently used as عاليسار (on the left).

examples.text: المكتبة موجودة على جهة اليسار بعد القوس.
examples.trans: The library is on the left side right after the arch.

examples.text: لفوا يسار عند النافورة بتلاقوا الممر.
examples.trans: Turn left at the fountain and you will find the passage.
